Let $N$ be the greatest four-digit positive integer such that changing any digit to 1 makes it divisible by 7.
Find $Q+R$ where $N = 1000Q + R$.

$N = 1000a + 100b + 10c + d$.
Conditions:
1. $1000(1) + 100b + 10c + d \equiv 0 \pmod 7$
2. $1000a + 100(1) + 10c + d \equiv 0 \pmod 7$
3. $1000a + 100b + 10(1) + d \equiv 0 \pmod 7$
4. $1000a + 100b + 10c + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod 7$

Let $N \equiv r \pmod 7$.
1. $N - 1000(a-1) \equiv 0 \pmod 7 \implies r \equiv 1000(a-1) \pmod 7$
2. $N - 100(b-1) \equiv 0 \pmod 7 \implies r \equiv 100(b-1) \pmod 7$
3. $N - 10(c-1) \equiv 0 \pmod 7 \implies r \equiv 10(c-1) \pmod 7$
4. $N - (d-1) \equiv 0 \pmod 7 \implies r \equiv (d-1) \pmod 7$

$1000 \equiv 6 \pmod 7$
$100 \equiv 2 \pmod 7$
$10 \equiv 3 \pmod 7$
$1 \equiv 1 \pmod 7$

So:
$r \equiv 6(a-1) \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 2(b-1) \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 3(c-1) \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 1(d-1) \pmod 7$

Solving for digits:
$a-1 \equiv 6^{-1}r \equiv 6r \pmod 7 \implies a \equiv 6r+1 \pmod 7$
$b-1 \equiv 2^{-1}r \equiv 4r \pmod 7 \implies b \equiv 4r+1 \pmod 7$
$c-1 \equiv 3^{-1}r \equiv 5r \pmod 7 \implies c \equiv 5r+1 \pmod 7$
$d-1 \equiv 1^{-1}r \equiv r \pmod 7 \implies d \equiv r+1 \pmod 7$

Now use $N \equiv 6a + 2b + 3c + d \equiv r \pmod 7$:
$r \equiv 6(6r+1) + 2(4r+1) + 3(5r+1) + (r+1) \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 36r + 6 + 8r + 2 + 15r + 3 + r + 1 \pmod 7$
$r \equiv (36+8+15+1)r + (6+2+3+1) \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 60r + 12 \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 4r + 5 \pmod 7$
$-3r \equiv 5 \pmod 7$
$4r \equiv 5 \pmod 7$
$r \equiv 3 \pmod 7$ (since $4 \times 3 = 12 \equiv 5$)

Digits:
$a \equiv 6(3)+1 = 19 \equiv 5 \pmod 7 \implies a \in \{5\}$
$b \equiv 4(3)+1 = 13 \equiv 6 \pmod 7 \implies b \in \{6\}$
$c \equiv 5(3)+1 = 16 \equiv 2 \pmod 7 \implies c \in \{2, 9\}$
$d \equiv 3+1 = 4 \pmod 7 \implies d \in \{4\}$

Greatest $N$: $a=5, b=6, c=9, d=4 \implies N = 5694$.
$Q = 5, R = 694$.
$Q+R = 699$.
